A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Draft-based Approximate Inference work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original RULER, LongBench, and MileBench evaluations, attention-correlation experiments, ablations, and latency and memory measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds cascade, cross-family, importance-estimation, and extended efficiency experiments.

M1.justification: v3 introduces SpecKV-PC, which compresses the prompt with SpecPC before applying SpecKV to the target KV cache, using shared draft information (Section 4.3). It also adds cross-family adaptations involving retokenization, word-level importance aggregation, and chat-template replacement (Appendix E.5). The original standalone algorithms remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 RULER tasks, included English/code LongBench tasks, and six temporal/semantic MileBench datasets. The added cross-family and output-length experiments use retained tasks with different model configurations or controls; they do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds LAQ++ throughout the KV comparisons. Existing large-model experiments gain H2O and PyramidKV comparisons, plus SpecPrefill and, in selected comparisons, LLMLingua-2, beyond v2's narrower SnapKV/CPC/R2C sets. StreamingLLM and AdaKV remain in the smaller-model appendix comparisons rather than being removed.

E3.justification: Efficiency evaluation changes from H100/Qwen2.5-14B time-to-first-token measurements to H200/Qwen2.5-32B generation timing, including 64–512 output-token sweeps. v3 also adds cross-family and oracle-importance protocols, varies cascade compression strength, and replaces the Qwen72B SpecKV draft configurations with 1.5B. Larger target models already appeared in v2's appendix.

E4.justification: v3 adds output-error versus accuracy tests, importance-correlation versus downstream-score analyses, cross-family robustness tests, cascade compression sensitivity, and stage-level efficiency breakdowns. It extends the lookahead ablation through EOS and adds a zero-lookahead SpecKV control. The earlier needle heatmap and multi-family mean/max attention-correlation suite are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both report benchmark point estimates and R-squared correlations. Additional correlation plots and dataset sample counts do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many matched LongBench scores are retained: Llama70B/3B SpecKV at Cmax=256 remains 48.80. v3 adds 51.60 for SpecKV-PC-2048 and 48.43 for LAQ++ in that comparison (Table 2), alongside cross-family, correlation, and new efficiency results. Qwen72B SpecKV entries are replaced under different draft settings, preventing direct performance-change attribution.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–3 and their Appendix B proofs are substantively retained. Table 1 corrects prompt-prefill complexity from O(Cmax) to O(Cmax^2) and adds prefill-space bounds. Section 3.1 introduces a centroid-distance proxy while explicitly distinguishing it from Theorem 1's token-wise error condition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the contributions to include SpecKV-PC and its combined accuracy, latency, and memory benefits. They also reframe the framework as unifying and extending recent lookahead work, narrowing the earlier broad novelty positioning. The central draft-based importance-estimation claim remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of cascade pre-filtering, failures under aggressive prompt compression, and SpecPC's sensitivity to cross-family attention mismatch. It explicitly requires a reasonably accurate draft and distinguishes the empirical centroid proxy from the theorem's assumptions. Earlier discussion favoring mean correlation versus max retrieval aggregation is removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents LAQ++ hyperparameters and the authors' own implementation, cross-tokenizer processing, and settings for the new H200 timing experiments. Most original pseudocode, implementation-stack information, and hyperparameters remain. The public code link is retained; the added reproducibility statement does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: LAQ++ becomes a central related method, with Sections 2–4 distinguishing SpecKV from its target-generated queries and full-cache requirement. v3 explicitly unifies LAQ++ and SpecPrefill and drops the broad claim of being first to use drafts for target-model approximate inference. GPT-3 and gpt-oss citations are added; the distillation citation is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, framework discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Theoretical motivations move into Sections 3.1–3.2, methods are consolidated under Section 4, and Appendix E is substantially reorganized. v3 also adds an appendix contents page, reproducibility statement, and LLM-usage disclosure.

P2.justification: The framework figure gains a performance panel, the SpecKV schematic is redrawn, and a cascade schematic is added. Main LongBench results use a combined table, while memory and latency share a redesigned figure. New correlation grids and stacked timing plots, expanded ablation axes, revised palettes, and ICLR formatting substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central accuracy–efficiency argument through the directly relevant LAQ++ comparison, tests linking importance-estimation quality to accuracy, and end-to-end timing with stage-level overhead analysis. Cascade sensitivity and cross-family experiments also expose useful applicability limits. These gains outweigh removal of the older mean/max correlation diagnostics. Reporting weaknesses remain: Section 5.1 names a 14B Qwen target while Figure 5 and Table 2 show 32B, and some superiority claims exceed what individual table entries support.
